title: Jan. 6, Part 2: Liz Cheney’s Battle Against the 'Big Lie'

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 届时，您可以观看其中一些毫无保留、未经修饰的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上免费直播部分精选采访，供所有人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Our country has had enough.
sentences.zh: 我们的国家已经受够了。

sentences.en: We will not take it anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们不会再忍气吞声了。

sentences.en: And that's what this is all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是这一切的意义所在。

sentences.en: And to use a favorite term that all of you people really came up with, we will stop the steal.
sentences.zh: 用你们这些人想出的一个最喜欢的词来说，我们要阻止窃选。

sentences.en: In the early afternoon of January 6th, when the president went on the National Mall to rally his supporters, he called out a small handful of Republicans by name.
sentences.zh: 1月6日下午早些时候，当总统前往国家广场集结他的支持者时，他点名了几位共和党人。

sentences.en: And Mike Pence, I hope you're going to stand up for the good of our Constitution and for the good of our country.
sentences.zh: 迈克·彭斯，我希望你能为了我们的宪法和国家的利益挺身而出。

sentences.en: And if you're not, I'm going to be very disappointed in you, I will tell you right now.
sentences.zh: 如果你不这样做，我会对你非常失望，我现在就告诉你。

sentences.en: Republicans who, for years, had stood by him, but now were rejecting his efforts to overturn the election.
sentences.zh: 那些多年来一直支持他，但现在却拒绝他推翻选举企图的共和党人。

sentences.en: And we've got to get rid of the weak congresspeople, the ones that aren't any good, the Liz Cheneys of the world.
sentences.zh: 我们必须除掉那些软弱的国会议员，那些毫无用处的家伙，比如世界上的利兹·切尼们。

sentences.en: We've got to get rid of them.
sentences.zh: 我们必须除掉他们。

sentences.en: We've got to get rid of them.
sentences.zh: 我们必须除掉他们。

sentences.en: Among them was Representative Liz Cheney of Wyoming, the number three Republican in the House,
sentences.zh: 其中包括怀俄明州众议员利兹·切尼，她是众议院排名第三的共和党人，

sentences.en: the daughter of a Republican vice president, and the only Republican leader telling the president to move on.
sentences.zh: 也是一位共和党副总统的女儿，更是唯一一位告诉总统该向前看的共和党领导人。

sentences.en: We're going to walk down to the Capitol, and we're going to cheer on our brave senators and congressmen and women.
sentences.zh: 我们要步行前往国会大厦，我们要为我们勇敢的参议员和国会议员们加油助威。

sentences.en: And we're probably not going to be cheering so much for some of them, because you'll never take back our country with weakness.
sentences.zh: 我们可能不会为其中一些人加油，因为软弱永远无法夺回我们的国家。

sentences.en: You have to show strength and you have to be strong.
sentences.zh: 你必须展现力量，你必须变得强大。

sentences.en: Cheney is among the last Republicans still in office who continues to criticize Trump's actions and seek accountability.
sentences.zh: 切尼是目前仍在任的最后几位继续批评特朗普行为并寻求问责的共和党人之一。

sentences.en: Today, in part two of our look at the legacy of January 6th, a conversation with Congresswoman Cheney.
sentences.zh: 今天，在我们回顾1月6日遗产的第二部分中，我们将与切尼众议员进行对话。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, January 6th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月6日，星期四。

sentences.en: Can you guys hear me?
sentences.zh: 你们能听到我说话吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Good afternoon, Congresswoman.
sentences.zh: 下午好，众议员。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Very well.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: So, Congressman, thank you for making time for us.
sentences.zh: 那么，众议员，感谢您抽出时间接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们非常感激。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Great to be with you guys.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你们在一起。

sentences.en: I want to start by going back with you to January 6th, so a year ago.
sentences.zh: 我想先带您回到一年前的1月6日。

sentences.en: And that morning, on the National Mall, the president, Donald Trump, has directly invoked your name to his supporters just before they stormed the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 那天早上，在国家广场上，唐纳德·特朗普总统在支持者冲击国会大厦前，直接向他们提到了您的名字。

sentences.en: And my understanding is that shortly after that, you get a call from your father, and he tells you about this fact.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，在那之后不久，您接到了父亲的电话，他告诉了您这件事。

sentences.en: Can you tell us about that?
sentences.zh: 能跟我们说说当时的情况吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I had gone over to the House floor because I was going to speak in support of county electoral votes and of the certification.
sentences.zh: 是的，当时我去了众议院议事厅，因为我准备发言支持各州的选举人票和认证结果。

sentences.en: And so I was actually in the cloakroom, the Republican cloakroom off the House floor, and my dad called and told me that the president had mentioned me.
sentences.zh: 我当时实际上是在众议院议事厅外的共和党休息室里，我父亲打电话告诉我总统提到了我。

sentences.en: And we had a conversation about the security implications of that and whether or not it would have an impact on my decision that I was going to speak.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了这背后的安全隐患，以及这是否会影响我原本打算发言的决定。

sentences.en: And, you know, we decided that it shouldn't prevent me from speaking, that it was very important to go ahead with that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们认为这不应该阻止我发言，继续进行下去非常重要。

sentences.en: But it was obviously, you know,
sentences.zh: 但这显然，你知道，

sentences.en: a jarring conversation to be having in the cloakroom of the House representatives with my dad about whether what the president of the United States had said was cause for concern for my security.
sentences.zh: 在众议院休息室里和父亲讨论美国总统所说的话是否会对我的安全构成威胁，这是一种令人不安的对话。

sentences.en: Well, of course, not long after that phone call, the president's supporters stormed the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 当然，在那通电话后不久，总统的支持者就冲击了国会大厦。

sentences.en: And it has been reported that on that day, a member of the Freedom Caucus and a House Republican colleague of yours, Jim Jordan,
sentences.zh: 据报道，那天，自由党团成员、您的众议院共和党同事吉姆·乔丹，

sentences.en: was standing in the aisle as members of Congress were being escorted away from the mob, from the protesters.
sentences.zh: 在国会议员们被护送离开暴徒和抗议者时，正站在过道上。

sentences.en: And that he said something to you, he said, we need to get the ladies away from the aisle, let me help you.
sentences.zh: 据说他对您说了些话，他说：“我们需要让女士们离开过道，让我来帮你们。”

sentences.en: And you are reported to have pushed his hand away and said to him, and I'm, you know, going to use this word because it was published, get away from me.
sentences.zh: 据报道，您推开了他的手，并对他说——你知道，我要用这个词，因为它已经被公开报道了——“离我远点”。

sentences.en: You fucking did this.
sentences.zh: “是你他妈干的。”

sentences.en: Can you confirm that story?
sentences.zh: 您能证实这个故事吗？

sentences.en: Because I think it's important.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为这很重要。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，是真的。

sentences.en: It's true.
sentences.zh: 是真的。

sentences.en: You know, I was in the aisle, on the aisle, and he came over to me, you know, and basically said, we need to get the ladies away from the aisle.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我当时在过道上，他走过来，基本上说我们需要让女士们离开过道。

sentences.en: And, you know, I had watched for the months since the election what was going on and the lies that had been told to people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，选举后的几个月里，我一直在观察发生的事情，以及那些对人们散布的谎言。

sentences.en: And, you know, it was both that I, you know, certainly didn't need his help.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一方面我当然不需要他的帮助。

sentences.en: And secondly, I thought clearly that the lie that they had been spreading and telling people had absolutely contributed to what we were living through at that moment.
sentences.zh: 其次，我认为很明显，他们一直在散布和告诉人们的谎言，绝对助长了我们当时所经历的一切。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's going to be months, Congressman, before your commission learns the details of Jim Jordan's involvement that day,
sentences.zh: 众议员，您的委员会还需要几个月的时间才能了解吉姆·乔丹那天参与的细节，

sentences.en: that he had been coordinating with the White House and seeking ways to prevent the election from being certified that day.
sentences.zh: 即他一直在与白宫协调，并寻求阻止当天选举结果获得认证的方法。

sentences.en: But you're saying that already at that moment, you, on some level, held people like Congressman Jordan responsible for what was happening in real time.
sentences.zh: 但您是说，当时那一刻，您在某种程度上就已经认为像乔丹议员这样的人对正在发生的实时事件负有责任。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In the hours that followed that exchange with Congressman Jordan, I imagine you spending lots of time in close quarters with other lawmakers, and you're all talking.
sentences.zh: 在与乔丹议员发生那次交流后的几个小时里，我想象您和其他议员在狭小的空间里待了很长时间，你们都在交谈。

sentences.en: When you are able to confer with fellow Republicans, did you find in those early hours and days after January 6th that there is a widespread understanding that Republicans,
sentences.zh: 当您能够与共和党同僚商议时，在1月6日之后的最初几个小时和几天里，您是否发现大家普遍认为共和党人，

sentences.en: especially Republicans in your own chamber of Congress, are responsible for this, that they did contribute?
sentences.zh: 尤其是您所在国会党团的共和党人，对此负有责任，他们确实推波助澜了？

sentences.en: You know.
sentences.zh: 你知道。

sentences.en: That your view is shared by your colleagues.
sentences.zh: 您的观点是否得到了同事们的认同。

sentences.en: Well, I think that what we certainly shared was an understanding that Donald Trump was responsible.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们肯定都认同唐纳德·特朗普负有责任。

sentences.en: And I think you can see that absolutely in many of the, probably, you know, well, many of the public comments.
sentences.zh: 我想你绝对可以在许多，可能，你知道，嗯，许多公开评论中看到这一点。

sentences.en: Last week's violent attack on the Capitol was undemocratic.
sentences.zh: 上周对国会大厦的暴力袭击是不民主的。

sentences.en: Including by Kevin McCarthy.
sentences.zh: 包括凯文·麦卡锡在内。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The senior most House Republican.
sentences.zh: 众议院最高级别的共和党人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The president bears responsibility for Wednesday's attack on Congress by mob rioters.
sentences.zh: 总统对周三暴徒袭击国会的事件负有责任。

sentences.en: He should have immediately denounced the mob when he saw what was unfolding.
sentences.zh: 当他看到事态发展时，他本应立即谴责暴徒。

sentences.en: There's no question.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: None.
sentences.zh: 一点也不。

sentences.en: And Mitch McConnell, the Senate Majority Leader.
sentences.zh: 还有参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: President Trump is practically and morally responsible for provoking the events of the day.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统在道义上和实际上都应对煽动当天的事件负责。

sentences.en: No question about it.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: I believe we need to hold the president accountable.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们需要追究总统的责任。

sentences.en: The president's language and rhetoric crossed a line and it was reckless.
sentences.zh: 总统的言辞越界了，这是鲁莽的。

sentences.en: What the president did on January 6th to me is inexcusable.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，总统在1月6日的所作所为是不可原谅的。

sentences.en: He shouldn't have done it.
sentences.zh: 他不该那样做。

sentences.en: The president formed the mob.
sentences.zh: 总统组建了暴徒。

sentences.en: The president excited the mob.
sentences.zh: 总统煽动了暴徒。

sentences.en: The president addressed the mob.
sentences.zh: 总统向暴徒发表了讲话。

sentences.en: He was just a flame.
sentences.zh: 他就是那团火焰。

sentences.en: The president is unfit.
sentences.zh: 总统不称职。

sentences.en: All I can say is count me out.
sentences.zh: 我只能说，算我一个。

sentences.en: Enough is enough.
sentences.zh: 够了就是够了。

sentences.en: And we will certify the winner of the 2020 presidential election.
sentences.zh: 我们将认证2020年总统大选的获胜者。

sentences.en: And so, you know, what happened after that seemed to be a situation where people, you know, lost their courage, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在那之后发生的事情似乎是人们，你知道，失去了勇气，我想。

sentences.en: Lost their commitment to dealing, not everybody, but too many members, lost their commitment to dealing with the truth of what had happened and the danger of what had happened.
sentences.zh: 失去了面对真相的承诺，不是所有人，但太多的议员失去了面对所发生之事的真相以及所发生之事危险性的承诺。

sentences.en: And, you know, then you began to see efforts to whitewash it.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，你开始看到试图粉饰它的努力。

sentences.en: So, you know, that's something that's very difficult, frankly, to explain.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，坦率地说，这很难解释。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk more about that because publicly we could point to a number of moments that illustrate this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们多谈谈这一点，因为在公开场合，我们可以指出许多说明这一点的时刻。

sentences.en: But I wonder if, for you, there was a quieter,
sentences.zh: 但我不知道，对您来说，在1月6日之后的几天或几周里，是否有一个更安静、

sentences.en: more private moment in the days or weeks after January 6th where you personally realized that your party was not going to stand together on this.
sentences.zh: 更私人的时刻，让您个人意识到您的政党不会在这件事上团结一致。

sentences.en: And, in fact, that you were going to be more or less isolated within your party in condemning it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，您在谴责这件事上或多或少会被党内孤立。

sentences.en: I think it was – it evolved.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是——它在演变。

sentences.en: I mean, I think there were some major moments, you know, before the month of January was over, Kevin McCarthy had gone to Mar-a-Lago to basically rehabilitate Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为有一些重大时刻，你知道，在1月份结束之前，凯文·麦卡锡已经去了海湖庄园，基本上是为了重塑唐纳德·特朗普的形象。

sentences.en: That was, you know, inexplicable from my perspective.
sentences.zh: 从我的角度来看，那是不可理喻的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Did you have conversations of that nature with the Republican leadership, with Congressman McCarthy at the time?
sentences.zh: 当时您是否与共和党领导层，与麦卡锡议员进行过此类对话？

sentences.en: I mean, honest ones where you said just that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那种您直言不讳的诚恳对话？

sentences.en: Um, we, we all had a number of conversations.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们，我们都进行过多次对话。

sentences.en: I, I don't want to, you know, go too far in terms of revealing those, but, but, but we did, in fact, you know, have a number of conversations.
sentences.zh: 我，我不想，你知道，在透露这些内容方面走得太远，但是，但是，我们确实，你知道，进行过多次对话。

sentences.en: It wasn't – there was – nobody was unclear about where I stood.
sentences.zh: 并不是——没有人不清楚我的立场。

sentences.en: I'll, I'll just leave it at that.
sentences.zh: 我就说到这里。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And I guess you became clear on where they were starting to stand.
sentences.zh: 我想您也清楚了他们开始站在什么立场上。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Do you think that the dissolution of the party's agreement at first on what January 6th was had anything to do with the fact that very quickly,
sentences.zh: 您认为党内最初对1月6日事件性质的共识破裂，是否与以下事实有关：很快，

sentences.en: just a week or so after the siege of the Capitol, this became about a very big choice Republicans were going to have to be asked to take.
sentences.zh: 就在国会大厦被围攻一周左右后，这演变成了一个共和党人必须被迫做出重大选择的问题。

sentences.en: And that was whether or not to impeach the president for his role in that day.
sentences.zh: 那就是是否要因为总统在当天的角色而弹劾他。

sentences.en: It's occurred to me that in setting it up as a dichotomy like that, vote to impeach, vote not to impeach, it accelerated the party's breakup over this.
sentences.zh: 我想到，通过将其设定为一种二分法，即投票弹劾或投票不弹劾，这加速了政党在此事上的分裂。

sentences.en: Um, well, first of all, I think there's no question that we had to move articles of impeachment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我认为毫无疑问我们必须提出弹劾条款。

sentences.en: I don't think there was any choice.
sentences.zh: 我不认为有任何选择。

sentences.en: I think it was our duty to do that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我们的职责所在。

sentences.en: I think that the Senate should have convicted him.
sentences.zh: 我认为参议院本应判定他有罪。

sentences.en: I think that part of what happened was there was a moment where members of the Republican Party, particularly people in leadership,
sentences.zh: 我认为发生的部分原因是，共和党成员，特别是领导层的人，有一个时刻，

sentences.en: had to decide whether they were really going to lead or whether they were going to be bystanders.
sentences.zh: 必须决定他们是真的要领导，还是要做旁观者。

sentences.en: And I do think that there was a period of time in the immediate aftermath of the attack where if more people had decided to lead, we could have.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为在袭击发生后的紧接着的一段时间里，如果有更多人决定领导，我们本可以做到。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, if you look at the period of time in January, we could easily have said, look, you know, the House has voted its article of impeachment.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，如果你看看1月份的那段时间，我们本可以很容易地说，看，你知道，众议院已经投票通过了弹劾条款。

sentences.en: The Senate is having the trial.
sentences.zh: 参议院正在进行审判。

sentences.en: And we as Republicans need to get focused on the future.
sentences.zh: 而我们作为共和党人需要专注于未来。

sentences.en: We need to be focused on substance and policy and our concerns about the Biden administration's policies.
sentences.zh: 我们需要专注于实质内容、政策以及我们对拜登政府政策的关切。

sentences.zh: 特朗普呼吁挑战者在南卡罗来纳州与她竞选。

sentences.en: Trump calls for challengers to run against her in South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 三名共和党人参加了那场竞选，他们都引用她关于总统和1月6日的评论作为他们参选的理由。

sentences.en: Three Republicans enter that race, all of them citing her comments about the president in January 6th as their reason for running.
sentences.zh: 到了五月，在你被逐出领导层前后，她已经完全平息了对此事的批评，并致力于赢回特朗普的支持者基础。

sentences.en: By May, around the time you are being ousted from leadership, she has totally quieted her criticisms on the matter and is working to win back the Trump base.
sentences.zh: 作为其中的一部分，她是投票将你逐出领导层的人之一，似乎是为了她自己的政治生存。

sentences.en: And as part of that, she's one of the people who votes to remove you from leadership, seemingly for her own political survival.
sentences.zh: 那么，除了你之外，其他人是否开始看到在你所走的道路上没有政治前途？

sentences.en: So is everyone else other than you starting to see that there's no political path forward on the path that you are on?
sentences.zh: 看，我不想把所有的同事都归为一类，但我认为我们的选民选举我们，你知道，部分原因是，你知道，他们重视我们的判断。

sentences.en: Look, I don't want to group all of my colleagues in one basket, but I think that our constituents elect us, you know, in part because, you know, they value our judgment.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们有责任说出关于这些事情的真相，并认识到我们可以影响事件。

sentences.en: And so, you know, we have a duty to tell the truth about these things and to recognize that we can influence events.
sentences.zh: 我只是认为有太多的同事看到了我们这些投票支持弹劾的人所承受的痛苦，他们决定，你知道吗，

sentences.en: And I just think that there are too many of my colleagues who looked at the grief that those of us who voted to impeach, for example, were taking, and they decided, you know what,
sentences.zh: 我们只是，我们打算希望，我们只是尝试不去谈论发生了什么，不去谈论特朗普，并在这里保持低调。

sentences.en: that we just, we're going to hope, we're just going to try to not talk about what happened and not talk about Trump and sort of keep our heads down here.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，当这么多人这样做时，你最终会陷入一种选民不知道真相的境地，你知道，我只是，我认为这对国家来说是非常，

sentences.en: But the problem is when so many people do that, you end up in a situation where the voters don't know the truth in ways that, you know, I just, I think is very,
sentences.zh: 非常危险的。

sentences.en: very dangerous for the country.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想谈谈这样一个事实，当然，还有待观察，但我们现在可能正处于这样一个时刻，即直言不讳，用你的话说，

sentences.en: Well, I want to talk about the fact that it, of course, remains to be seen, but we now may be in a moment where speaking out, where, in your words,
sentences.zh: 做正确的事等同于失去你的席位。

sentences.en: doing the right thing is equivalent to losing your seat.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样的话，难道不是政党自己造成了这种现实吗？

sentences.en: And if that's the case, didn't the party cause that reality for itself?
sentences.zh: 过去几年有很多报道称，在闭门会议中，许多共和党政客会承认事情做得太过分了。

sentences.en: There's been a lot of reporting over the past few years about how behind closed doors, many Republican politicians will acknowledge that things have gone too far.
sentences.zh: 他们会承认特朗普正在损害政党。

sentences.en: They'll acknowledge that Trump is damaging the party.
sentences.zh: 他们会承认乔·拜登赢了，特朗普输了。

sentences.en: They'll acknowledge that Joe Biden won and Trump loSt.
sentences.zh: 我相信你自己也从许多同事那里听到过类似的话。

sentences.en: I'm sure you've heard from many of your colleagues yourself along these lines.
sentences.zh: 这几乎有一种感觉，哦，别担心，我们在公开场合这么说，但我们并不真正相信它们。

sentences.en: And it's almost got this quality of, oh, don't worry, we say these things in public, but we don't actually believe them.
sentences.zh: 但切尼众议员，这难道不是整个问题的所在吗？

sentences.en: But isn't that turning out to be, Congresswoman, the whole problem?
sentences.zh: 多年的同谋和允许总统的虚假主张不受挑战，导致了一个大多数共和党选民现在相信那个弥天大谎的现实。

sentences.en: That years of complicity and allowing the president's false claims to go unchallenged has resulted in a reality in which the majority of Republican voters now believe in the big lie.
sentences.zh: 难道正是因为政党太害怕公开挑战总统，才把你和政党带到了这一刻吗？

sentences.en: And isn't the very fact that the party was too afraid of publicly challenging the president what brought you and the party to this moment?
sentences.zh: 我当然认为在1月6日之后确实如此。

sentences.en: I certainly think that that is true post-January 6th.
sentences.zh: 你知道，看，在1月6日之前和选举之前，你知道，我在唐纳德·特朗普政策方面的投票记录，我大约93%的时间都投给了他。

sentences.en: You know, look, pre-January 6th and pre-the election, you know, my voting record in terms of, you know, Donald Trump's policies, I voted with him like 93% of the time.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果政党，嗯，如果民选官员不认真对待担任这些职务的真正意义，那么我们就处境糟糕了。

sentences.en: You know, if the party, well, if elected officials aren't going to take seriously what it really means to be in these offices, then we are in a bad place.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在共和党正在允许唐纳德·特朗普的毒素以及他所做的事情和他的谎言继续感染政党，而不去反对它。

sentences.en: And I think that right now the Republican Party is allowing the toxin of Donald Trump and what he did and his lies to continue to infect the party and not standing up against it.
sentences.zh: 我并没有低估站出来直言不讳所带来的困难和挑战。

sentences.en: And I don't minimize the difficulty and the challenges that come with standing up and speaking out.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不想那样做，那么你就不应该从事这些工作，因为，你知道，

sentences.en: But if you don't want to do that, then you shouldn't be in these jobs because, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们基本的结构和基本的系统依赖于有良知的人去做他们认为正确的事情。

sentences.en: our fundamental structure and fundamental system depends upon people of good faith doing what they believe is right.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果你只是为了当官而当选，

sentences.en: And, you know, if you're just going to get elected to office to say you're in the office,
sentences.zh: 但当关键时刻到来，当考验来临，而你不愿意做你知道是正确的事情时，那确实会产生系统崩溃的可能性。

sentences.en: but when the chips are down and when the test comes and you're unwilling to do what you know is right, that really does then create the potential that the system can unravel.
sentences.zh: 我认为每个人都必须认清自己在防止这种情况发生中所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: And I think everybody's got to come to grips with the role that they play in preventing that from happening.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你不知道电视画面是1月6日的视频，你真的会以为那是一次正常的游客访问。

sentences.en: You know, if you didn't know the TV footage was a video from January the 6th, you would actually think it was a normal tourist visit.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你不知道电视画面是1月6日的视频，你真的会以为那是一次正常的游客访问。

sentences.en: They're staying within the rope lines in the rotunda.
sentences.zh: 他们待在圆顶大厅的警戒线内。

sentences.en: That's not what an armed insurrection would look like.
sentences.zh: 那看起来可不像是一场武装叛乱。

sentences.en: Nancy Pelosi bears responsibility as Speaker of the House for the tragedy that occurred on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 作为众议院议长，南希·佩洛西对1月6日发生的悲剧负有责任。

sentences.en: Knives out for Cheney.
sentences.zh: 切尼成了众矢之的。

sentences.en: She is defiant.
sentences.zh: 她表现得很倔强。

sentences.en: Cheney's own voters despise her.
sentences.zh: 切尼自己的选民都鄙视她。

sentences.en: Her career in Congress is over.
sentences.zh: 她在国会的职业生涯结束了。

sentences.en: She is looking backwards.
sentences.zh: 她是在向后看。

sentences.en: Republicans are looking forward.
sentences.zh: 共和党人是在向前看。

sentences.en: To try to erase Donald Trump from the Republican Party is insane.
sentences.zh: 试图将唐纳德·特朗普从共和党中抹去是疯狂的。

sentences.en: And the people who try to erase him are going to wind up getting erased.
sentences.zh: 而那些试图抹去他的人，最终会被抹去。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 首次下载《纽约时报》应用，首月免费。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用，获取30天免费访问权限。

sentences.en: The House of Representatives voted today to form a special committee to investigate the January 6th attack on the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 众议院今天投票决定成立一个特别委员会，调查1月6日针对国会大厦的袭击事件。

sentences.en: The vote was 222 to 190.
sentences.zh: 投票结果是222票对190票。

sentences.en: All Democrats voted in favor and joining them, just two Republicans, Representatives Liz Cheney and Adam Kinzinger.
sentences.zh: 所有民主党人都投了赞成票，加入他们的只有两名共和党人，即众议员利兹·切尼和亚当·金辛格。

sentences.en: We want to find out what went on in the run-up to January 6th.
sentences.zh: 我们想查明1月6日之前发生了什么。

sentences.en: We want to find out what happened on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 我们想查明1月6日当天发生了什么。

sentences.en: We want to know what was going on in the White House and the administration.
sentences.zh: 我们想知道白宫和政府内部当时在发生什么。

sentences.en: If there were discussions about how to overturn the election.
sentences.zh: 如果当时有关于如何推翻选举的讨论的话。

sentences.en: As you can see, I am very proud to be able to announce the members of that committee this morning.
sentences.zh: 如你所见，我非常自豪能在今天早上宣布该委员会的成员。

sentences.en: Congresswoman Liz Cheney of the Armed Services Committee has patriotically agreed to serve on the committee.
sentences.zh: 来自军事委员会的国会议员利兹·切尼已爱国地同意在该委员会任职。

sentences.en: We're very honored and proud that she has agreed to serve on the committee.
sentences.zh: 她同意加入委员会，我们感到非常荣幸和自豪。

sentences.en: So this all brings us to the January 6th commission, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，这一切都把我们带到了1月6日调查委员会的问题上。

sentences.en: Soon after you are removed from Republican leadership and in defiance of Republican House leaders who have just ousted you,
sentences.zh: 在你被免去共和党领导职务后不久，且在刚刚将你赶下台的共和党众议院领导人的反对下，

sentences.en: you agree to serve as the number two on the Democratic-led special committee investigating January 6th.
sentences.zh: 你同意担任由民主党领导的1月6日调查特别委员会的二号人物。

sentences.en: And you are appointed by none other than House Speaker Nancy Pelosi.
sentences.zh: 而且你是由众议院议长南希·佩洛西亲自任命的。

sentences.en: Was that complicated for you at all?
sentences.zh: 这对你来说有什么复杂的地方吗？

sentences.en: That at the same moment your own party is turning away from you and strips you from power,
sentences.zh: 就在你所在的政党背弃你并剥夺你权力的时候，

sentences.en: the Democratic Party asks you to join them to take a leading role in what turns out to be their efforts to hold former President Trump responsible
sentences.zh: 民主党却邀请你加入他们，在他们旨在追究前总统特朗普责任的努力中发挥领导作用，

sentences.en: in a way that your party has now made clear that it will not be doing?
sentences.zh: 而你的政党已经明确表示不会这样做，这难道不复杂吗？

sentences.en: Well, I could not have imagined that that is where I would end up.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我无法想象我最终会走到这一步。

sentences.en: Um, and, you know, I, I certainly think it would have been preferable, for example, if we'd had a bipartisan commission.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我当然认为如果能有一个两党委员会会更好，例如。

sentences.en: I voted for that in the House.
sentences.zh: 我在众议院投了赞成票。

sentences.en: We had 35 Republicans who voted for, you know, a commission that looked like the 9-11 commission that was not made up of current House members
sentences.zh: 我们有35名共和党人投票支持，你知道，一个像9/11委员会那样不完全由现任众议员组成的委员会，

sentences.en: and was equal numbers Republicans and Democrats.
sentences.zh: 而且共和党和民主党人数相等。

sentences.en: But, you know, there, again, Leader McCarthy, you know, basically told the Republican-ranking member of the Homeland Security Committee,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，又是麦卡锡领袖，他基本上告诉国土安全委员会的共和党高级成员，

sentences.en: John Katko, who was one of the 10 who voted to impeach, told Katko to negotiate what a commission should look like with the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 约翰·卡特科，他是那10名投票弹劾的人之一，告诉卡特科去与民主党协商委员会应该是什么样子。

sentences.en: The Republicans got everything that we asked for, and then McCarthy pulled his support for the commission.
sentences.zh: 共和党人得到了我们要求的一切，然后麦卡锡撤回了对委员会的支持。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then it went over to the Senate, and McConnell wouldn't support it and lobbied against it in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 然后它到了参议院，麦康奈尔不支持它，并在参议院游说反对它。

sentences.en: So it failed in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 所以它在参议院失败了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we ended up in a situation where you cannot let January 6th go uninvestigated.
sentences.zh: 所以我们最终陷入了一种不能让1月6日事件不被调查的境地。

sentences.en: And the bipartisan commission has failed.
sentences.zh: 而两党委员会已经失败了。

sentences.en: So the only thing that's left is this select committee.
sentences.zh: 所以剩下的唯一选择就是这个特别委员会。

sentences.en: And so by the time we got to the select committee and I voted for the resolution that created it on the floor,
sentences.zh: 所以当我们最终成立特别委员会，并且我在众议院投票支持了创建它的决议时，

sentences.en: when Speaker Pelosi called and asked me to be on it, I didn't hesitate.
sentences.zh: 当佩洛西议长打电话邀请我加入时，我没有犹豫。

sentences.en: I just, I think it's, there's no way that you can justify not investigating the worst attack on our Capitol since the War of 1812.
sentences.zh: 我只是认为，对于自1812年战争以来对我们国会大厦最严重的袭击，如果不进行调查是无法辩解的。

sentences.en: And so I was honored to be asked, and I'm honored to be part of the committee.
sentences.zh: 所以我很荣幸受到邀请，也很荣幸能成为委员会的一员。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So a couple of weeks ago, we get some explosive news out of this commission.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我们从这个委员会得到了一些爆炸性的消息。

sentences.en: There is written textual evidence that some Republicans, including members of Congress, wanted to overrule or throw out the election results in 2020.
sentences.zh: 有书面文字证据表明，一些共和党人，包括国会议员，想要推翻或废除2020年的选举结果。

sentences.en: We see it in the just-released correspondence with former White House Chief of Staff Mark Meadows.
sentences.zh: 我们在刚刚公布的与前白宫幕僚长马克·梅多斯的通信中看到了这一点。

sentences.en: Involving former White House Chief of Staff Mark Meadows, who turns over some key communications to you all.
sentences.zh: 涉及前白宫幕僚长马克·梅多斯，他向你们移交了一些关键通讯记录。

sentences.en: Those communications reveal a direct role that Republicans and conservative leaders played in January 6th.
sentences.zh: 这些通讯揭示了共和党人和保守派领导人在1月6日事件中扮演的直接角色。

sentences.en: A Trump ally texts White House Chief of Staff Mark Meadows, here's an aggressive strategy.
sentences.zh: 一位特朗普的盟友给白宫幕僚长马克·梅多斯发短信说，这是一个激进的策略。

sentences.en: Why can't the states of Georgia, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, and other R-controlled state houses declare this is BS, where conflicts and election not called that night,
sentences.zh: 为什么佐治亚州、北卡罗来纳州、宾夕法尼亚州和其他共和党控制的州议会不能宣布这是胡扯，因为存在争议且选举当晚没有宣布结果，

sentences.en: and just send their own electors to vote and have it go to the Supreme Court?
sentences.zh: 然后直接派出他们自己的选举人去投票，并让它上交到最高法院？

sentences.en: Another lawmaker to Meadows, yesterday was a terrible day.
sentences.zh: 另一位议员对梅多斯说，昨天是糟糕的一天。

sentences.en: We tried everything we could in our objection to the six states.
sentences.zh: 我们在反对这六个州的投票中尝试了一切可能的方法。

sentences.en: I'm sorry nothing worked.
sentences.zh: 很抱歉什么都没奏效。

sentences.en: On January 5th, Congressman Jim Jordan sent Meadows a message, quote,
sentences.zh: 1月5日，众议员吉姆·乔丹给梅多斯发了一条信息，引用如下：

sentences.en: On January 6th, 2021, Vice President Mike Pence, as president of the Senate, should call out all electoral votes that he believes are unconstitutional as no electoral votes at all.
sentences.zh: 2021年1月6日，副总统迈克·彭斯作为参议院议长，应该宣布他认为违宪的所有选举人票根本不是选举人票。

sentences.en: And one of the key figures implicated is Jim Jordan, this man who, on January 6th, you turned to and said, you did this.
sentences.zh: 而涉及的关键人物之一就是吉姆·乔丹，就是这个人在1月6日那天，你转过身对他说，是你干的。

sentences.en: People like you did this.
sentences.zh: 像你这样的人干的。

sentences.en: So I wonder, as you learned these details about his role in all this, how you thought about what this evidence amounts to.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，当你了解到他在这一切中扮演角色的细节时，你是如何看待这些证据的意义的。

sentences.en: You have talked about your colleagues placating and allowing President Trump's behavior.
sentences.zh: 你谈到你的同事们安抚并纵容特朗普总统的行为。

sentences.en: But I think for many, what you all have revealed, for example, a message that Congressman Jordan passes on to Meadows
sentences.zh: 但我认为对许多人来说，你们所揭露的内容，例如乔丹议员传给梅多斯的信息，

sentences.en: about how Vice President Pence could discount electoral votes, just kind of toss them aside, that doesn't just feel like placating or allowing.
sentences.zh: 关于副总统彭斯如何能够折算选举人票，直接把它们扔到一边，这不仅仅感觉像是安抚或纵容。

sentences.en: It feels like a kind of effort to collaborate in overturning the election.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是一种在推翻选举中进行协作的努力。

sentences.en: And so from what you've seen so far, did some of your Republican colleagues,
sentences.zh: 所以根据你目前所看到的，是否有一些你的共和党同事，

sentences.en: and I'm not sure what the right word would be for this, and maybe you haven't put your finger on it either,
sentences.zh: 我不确定用什么词来形容比较合适，也许你也没想好，

sentences.en: but did they perhaps participate in something approaching sedition or treason?
sentences.zh: 但他们是否可能参与了接近煽动叛乱或叛国的事情？

sentences.en: Well, I don't want to say that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不想那么说。

sentences.en: I don't want to go that far.
sentences.zh: 我不想走那么远。

sentences.en: I think those are obviously very, very serious charges.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些显然是非常、非常严重的指控。

sentences.en: And I certainly don't want to make those kinds of claiMs.
sentences.zh: 我当然不想做出那种断言。

sentences.en: I think that the committee is clearly looking at all of the different pieces of the effort to overturn the election,
sentences.zh: 我认为委员会显然正在审视推翻选举努力的所有不同部分，

sentences.en: all of the different pieces, the effort to delay the electoral vote, the efforts to pressure local government officials.
sentences.zh: 所有不同的部分，推迟选举人投票的努力，向地方政府官员施压的努力。

sentences.en: So I, again, I think the facts will lead where they go.
sentences.zh: 所以我再次认为，事实会引导我们走向真相。

sentences.en: I'm not making the kinds of claims that you made, but I think any effort to substitute, you know, the judgment of Congress for the judgment of the people of the states
sentences.zh: 我没有做出你所做的那种断言，但我认为任何试图用国会的判断来取代各州人民的判断，

sentences.en: and selecting the president, in my view, was unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 在选择总统这件事上，在我看来，都是违宪的。

sentences.en: And, of course, we saw ultimately what happened when people were lied to and summoned to Washington.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们最终看到了当人们被欺骗并被召集到华盛顿时发生了什么。

sentences.en: So it's now been exactly one year since January 6th.
sentences.zh: 所以距离1月6日正好过去了一年。

sentences.en: And I want to talk about where things stand for you and the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈你和共和党目前的处境。

sentences.en: Because not only are you increasingly alone in continuing to insist on accountability for that day within your party,
sentences.zh: 因为你不仅在坚持要求追究那一天责任的问题上在党内越来越孤立，

sentences.en: a pretty shocking statistic has emerged, that one-third of Republicans running for Congress in the coming year are running on some version of the big lie,
sentences.zh: 而且出现了一个相当令人震惊的统计数据，即明年竞选国会议员的共和党人中，有三分之一的人是在宣扬某种版本的“弥天大谎”，

sentences.en: that the election was stolen from President Trump.
sentences.zh: 即选举是从特朗普总统手中偷走的。

sentences.en: There's no question, and it's widely reported, that there was widespread fraud and irregularities across this country.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，而且有广泛报道称，这个国家存在广泛的欺诈和违规行为。

sentences.en: Many of us were warning about the fact that the Democrats unilaterally fundamentally altered our voting system inside 90 days.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人当时就在警告，民主党人在90天内单方面从根本上改变了我们的投票系统。

sentences.en: We warned that the state of Nevada was just simply not ready to give us a fully fair and secure election.
sentences.zh: 我们警告说，内华达州根本没有准备好给我们一场完全公平和安全的选举。

sentences.en: Who in this room doubts that Google would like to swing a presidential election?
sentences.zh: 在这个房间里，谁怀疑谷歌想要左右总统大选？

sentences.en: Well, who's to say they didn't?
sentences.zh: 嗯，谁又能说他们没这么做呢？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't want to make a baseless claim, but I don't have access to Google's changes in their master search-up rooMs.
sentences.zh: 我不想做出毫无根据的指控，但我无法接触到谷歌主搜索室的更改记录。

sentences.en: If I was a United States senator on the day of the certification, I would have stood with Senator Cruz and Senator Scott
sentences.zh: 如果我是认证当天的美国参议员，我会和克鲁兹参议员和斯科特参议员站在一起，

sentences.en: and that small handful of senators who had the courage to stand up and say, wait, let's hold up on the certification of this election.
sentences.zh: 和那一小撮有勇气站出来说“等等，让我们暂停这次选举的认证”的参议员站在一起。

sentences.en: And what that says to me is that not only is the party no longer condemning what happened, in fact, its identity is solidifying around it.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说意味着，该党不仅不再谴责所发生的事情，事实上，它的身份认同正围绕着它而固化。

sentences.en: And, of course, unsurprisingly, given the amount you've spoken out, one of the races this fall that now features this dynamic is yours, your re-election in Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 当然，不出所料，鉴于你发表了这么多言论，今年秋天出现这种动态的竞选之一就是你的，你在怀俄明州的连任竞选。

sentences.en: Liz Cheney doesn't know what writing for the brand means.
sentences.zh: 利兹·切尼不知道为品牌效力意味着什么。

sentences.en: We sent her to D.C.
sentences.zh: 我们把她送到华盛顿，

sentences.en: to be loyal to the outfit that hired her, to be loyal to Wyoming and our values.
sentences.zh: 是为了忠于雇佣她的机构，忠于怀俄明州和我们的价值观。

sentences.en: Instead of fighting for us, she's fighting against President Trump.
sentences.zh: 她没有为我们而战，却在与特朗普总统作对。

sentences.en: She betrayed us.
sentences.zh: 她背叛了我们。

sentences.en: She betrayed our values.
sentences.zh: 她背叛了我们的价值观。

sentences.en: She betrayed the brand.
sentences.zh: 她背叛了这个品牌。

sentences.en: You now face a Republican primary challenger who seems to embody
sentences.zh: 你现在面临一位共和党初选挑战者，她似乎体现了

sentences.en: much of this new version of the Republican Party that you have been so critical of.
sentences.zh: 你一直强烈批评的共和党新版本的许多特征。

sentences.en: Right now, the most important job Republicans have in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 现在，共和党人在华盛顿最重要的工作，

sentences.en: is to stop Nancy Pelosi and the radical Democrats from destroying our country.
sentences.zh: 就是阻止南希·佩洛西和激进的民主党人摧毁我们的国家。

sentences.en: I'm Harriet Hageman, and I know what it means to ride for the brands.
sentences.zh: 我是哈丽特·哈格曼，我知道为品牌效力意味着什么。

sentences.en: And President Trump has endorsed her and encouraged voters in Wyoming to see her as a vehicle for ousting you from Congress.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统已经支持了她，并鼓励怀俄明州的选民将她视为将你赶出国会的工具。

sentences.en: And from the conversations we've had with our colleagues and political analysts, it looks like you could be in for a pretty tough race this fall.
sentences.zh: 根据我们与同事和政治分析人士的谈话，看起来你今年秋天可能会面临一场相当艰难的竞选。

sentences.en: In fact, one of our colleagues tells us, so far, and please correct me if I'm wrong, you're not doing some of the typical things a candidate does ahead of re-election.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们的一位同事告诉我们，到目前为止，如果我错了请纠正我，你并没有做一些候选人在连任前通常会做的事情。

sentences.en: So are you intending to seek re-election?
sentences.zh: 那么你打算寻求连任吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对。

sentences.en: And I'm not sure which of your colleagues, what they're talking about, but I am absolutely committed to my re-election in Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 我不确定你的哪位同事在说什么，但我绝对致力于我在怀俄明州的连任。

sentences.en: And I welcome the race that you've described.
sentences.zh: 我欢迎你所描述的这场竞选。

sentences.en: I think that it will be an opportunity for the people of Wyoming to decide whether, you know, they want to cast their vote for somebody
sentences.zh: 我认为这将是怀俄明州人民决定他们是否想把票投给某人的机会，

sentences.en: who's pledged allegiance to Donald Trump over allegiance to the Constitution and, frankly, to the people of Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 一个比起对宪法、坦率地说，比起对怀俄明州人民的忠诚，更宣誓效忠唐纳德·特朗普的人。

sentences.en: So it's going to be an exciting race, but it's one I'm very much looking forward to and engaged in and intend to prevail.
sentences.zh: 所以这将是一场激动人心的竞选，但我非常期待并投入其中，并打算获胜。

sentences.en: Well, prevailing depends in part on the idea that voters are still willing to support this version of a Republican candidate like you
sentences.zh: 嗯，获胜在一定程度上取决于选民是否仍然愿意支持像你这样的共和党候选人版本，

sentences.en: and break this cycle that's been created in the party.
sentences.zh: 并打破党内形成的这种循环。

sentences.en: I still question if it's now too late for that to be possible within the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 我仍然怀疑在共和党内部是否还有可能做到这一点。

sentences.en: Let's presume for a minute that the party wants to get out of this cycle, this cycle in which it's now in many ways afraid of its own voters,
sentences.zh: 让我们假设一下，如果该党想要摆脱这种循环，这种在许多方面害怕自己选民的循环，

sentences.en: afraid to challenge their beliefs that the 2020 election was stolen.
sentences.zh: 害怕挑战他们关于2020年选举被窃取的信念。

sentences.en: A belief that Republican politicians undeniably helped to establish and uphold in the first place.
sentences.zh: 一种共和党政客不可否认地帮助建立并首先维护的信念。

sentences.en: Those voters now control the party through their votes.
sentences.zh: 这些选民现在通过他们的选票控制着该党。

sentences.en: If, again, the party wants to, how does it even go about possibly breaking free of this cycle?
sentences.zh: 如果，再次强调，该党想要这样做，它该如何着手打破这个循环呢？

sentences.en: You know, I believe fundamentally that the vast majority of Americans,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我从根本上相信绝大多数美国人，

sentences.en: Republicans and Democrats,
sentences.zh: 无论是共和党人还是民主党人，

sentences.en: want to live in a country that continues to be characterized by the freedoms that we enjoy and that they are fundamentally faithful to the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 都希望生活在一个继续以我们享有的自由为特征的国家，并且他们从根本上忠于宪法。

sentences.en: And I think of it less as, you know, what the party has to do and more about what we all have to do as Americans together, because it's a dangerous moment.
sentences.zh: 我认为这与其说是党必须做什么，不如说是我们作为美国人共同必须做什么，因为这是一个危险的时刻。

sentences.en: The stakes are really high.
sentences.zh: 利害攸关，非常严重。

sentences.en: If Donald Trump becomes the Republican nominee, if Donald Trump is elected president again, I think that the Republic is at risk.
sentences.zh: 如果唐纳德·特朗普成为共和党提名人，如果唐纳德·特朗普再次当选总统，我认为共和国就处于危险之中。

sentences.en: And the notion that someone who has shown as little commitment to the Constitution as he did would be entrusted with its preservation once again
sentences.zh: 而那种认为一个对宪法表现出如此少承诺的人，会被再次委托去维护它，

sentences.en: is something that, you know, I think we have to avoid at all costs.
sentences.zh: 是我认为我们必须不惜一切代价避免的事情。

sentences.en: And that means demanding of your elected officials that they act with faith to the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要求你们选出的官员以忠于宪法的方式行事。

sentences.en: And that means every individual American themselves doing what you know is right and making sure you're supporting people who are going to do the right thing,
sentences.zh: 这意味着每一位美国个人都要做你知道正确的事情，并确保你支持那些会做正确事情的人，

sentences.en: even when it's tough, even when it's difficult.
sentences.zh: 即使在困难的时候，即使在艰难的时候。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But how do you do it?
sentences.zh: 但你该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: I mean, how do you see your way out of a cycle in which it now appears the voters control the party and the voters believe an election was stolen?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你如何找到出路，摆脱一个现在看来选民控制着政党，且选民相信选举被窃取的循环？

sentences.en: I think a lot of people see it as very difficult to find a way out of that dynamic.
sentences.zh: 我认为很多人觉得很难找到摆脱这种动态关系的方法。

sentences.en: Well, I refuse to believe and won't sit by and watch our system be unraveled.
sentences.zh: 但我拒绝相信这一点，也不会坐视我们的体制分崩离析。

sentences.en: And I think that the effort to make sure that we, as I said, elect people who are faithful to the Constitution, people who will defend the system, stand up against the lie,
sentences.zh: 我认为，正如我所说，我们要确保选出忠于宪法、捍卫体制、敢于对抗谎言的人，

sentences.en: all of those things matter hugely.
sentences.zh: 所有这些努力都至关重要。

sentences.en: You believe that continuing to speak the truth and stand up for what you believe, somehow that will win out.
sentences.zh: 你相信坚持说真话、坚持自己的信仰，最终会胜出。

sentences.en: And hopefully you think that will happen before the democracy collapses.
sentences.zh: 也希望你认为这会在民主崩溃之前发生。

sentences.en: I know that it is my responsibility and my duty and my obligation, and I'm going to continue doing it because I know it's what's right.
sentences.zh: 我知道这是我的责任、职责和义务，我会继续这样做，因为我知道这是正确的。

sentences.en: And I believe fundamentally in the goodness of the vast majority of the American people and in the greatness of this country.
sentences.zh: 我从根本上相信绝大多数美国人民的善良，也相信这个国家的伟大。

sentences.en: And I'm not going to cede our party and I'm not going to cede the Republic to Donald Trump or those forces who, you know, have shown themselves unfit
sentences.zh: 我不会把我们的党拱手让人，也不会把共和国拱手让给唐纳德·特朗普或那些已经证明自己不称职的势力，

sentences.en: and have shown themselves unwilling to carry out their duties to the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 他们已经证明自己不愿履行对宪法的职责。

sentences.en: And if they cede you, what happens?
sentences.zh: 如果他们把你踢出局，会发生什么？

sentences.en: If they say, Congresswoman, we appreciate your service
sentences.zh: 如果他们说，女议员，我们感谢您的服务，

sentences.en: and we like that you stood up for what you think is right, but ultimately we expel you from our party and from your seat in Congress
sentences.zh: 我们赞赏您坚持自己的正确立场，但最终我们还是要把您逐出党派和国会席位，

sentences.en: as a result of everything you've done, then where will that leave you?
sentences.zh: 作为您所作所为的结果，那您会处于什么境地？

sentences.en: And how will you view this all?
sentences.zh: 您又会如何看待这一切？

sentences.en: Look, I do not anticipate that's going to happen, but there's no choice here.
sentences.zh: 看，我不认为会发生那种事，但我们别无选择。

sentences.en: Well, Congresswoman, we want to thank you very much for your time.
sentences.zh: 好的，女议员，非常感谢您抽出时间。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们不胜感激。

sentences.en: Well, great to be with you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能与您交谈。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I appreciate being on.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能参加节目。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Good luck to you.
sentences.zh: 祝你好运。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: The Times reports that Donald Trump is preparing to hold a series of events intended to establish himself as a key player in the 2022 midterms
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》报道称，唐纳德·特朗普正准备举办一系列活动，旨在确立自己作为2022年中期选举关键人物的地位，

sentences.en: and possibly lay the groundwork for another presidential run in 2024.
sentences.zh: 并可能为2024年的再次竞选总统奠定基础。

sentences.en: Among the events is a forum at Mar-a-Lago which will bring together candidates whom Trump is endorsing in the midterms,
sentences.zh: 这些活动包括在海湖庄园举行的一场论坛，届时将汇集特朗普在中期选举中支持的候选人，

sentences.en: including Harriet Hageman, who is challenging Liz Cheney in Wyoming tomorrow in part three of our series, a check-in on the state of American democracy.
sentences.zh: 其中包括哈丽特·哈格曼，她明天将在怀俄明州挑战利兹·切尼。这是我们系列报道的第三部分，关注美国民主现状。

sentences.en: One year after January 6th.
sentences.zh: 1月6日事件一周年之际。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Chicago's public school system, the nation's third largest, was shut down on Wednesday over a dispute between the city and its teachers' union
sentences.zh: 周三，全美第三大公立学校系统——芝加哥公立学校系统因市政府与教师工会之间的纠纷而关闭，

sentences.en: over teachers' safety amid surging infections from the Omicron variant.
sentences.zh: 纠纷焦点在于奥密克戎变异株感染激增期间教师的安全问题。

sentences.en: Teachers had voted not to show up to work, despite pleas from the city's mayor, Lori Lightfoot, who said that classrooms are safe
sentences.zh: 尽管芝加哥市长洛里·莱特富特恳求教师们复工，并称教室是安全的，但教师们仍投票决定罢工，

sentences.en: and has accused the teachers of an illegal work stoppage.
sentences.zh: 市长指责教师们进行了非法停工。

sentences.en: There's no reason to shut down the entire system, particularly given the catastrophic consequences that will flow.
sentences.zh: 没有理由关闭整个系统，特别是考虑到随之而来的灾难性后果。

sentences.en: One week, two weeks, it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 一周也好，两周也罢，这都不重要。

sentences.en: And Mr. Djokovic failed to provide appropriate evidence to meet the entry requirements to Australia, and visa has been subsequently cancelled.
sentences.zh: 德约科维奇先生未能提供符合澳大利亚入境要求的相关证明，其签证随后被取消。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, the world's number one tennis player, Novak Djokovic, was denied entry into Australia, where he had just arrived and was scheduled to compete in the Australian Open
sentences.zh: 周三，世界排名第一的网球选手诺瓦克·德约科维奇被拒绝入境澳大利亚，他刚抵达那里，原计划参加澳大利亚网球公开赛，

sentences.en: because he has refused to be vaccinated against COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 原因是他拒绝接种新冠疫苗。

sentences.en: The decision prompted fury from Djokovic's home country of Serbia, but Australian officials said that it was consistent with its vaccination policies for Australians.
sentences.zh: 这一决定引发了德约科维奇祖国塞尔维亚的愤怒，但澳大利亚官员表示，这符合其针对澳大利亚人的疫苗接种政策。

sentences.en: And it's not unreasonable to have exactly the same requirements of all who enter this country.
sentences.zh: 对所有入境本国的人提出同样的要求并非不合理。

sentences.en: So fair and equitable for all.
sentences.zh: 这对所有人来说都是公平合理的。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由杰西卡·钟、罗布·齐普科、雷切尔·奎斯特和埃里克·克鲁普克制作，戴安娜·阮提供了协助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Tobin, contains original music by Chelsea Daniel, Dan Powell, and Marian Lozano, and engineered by Corey Schreppel.
sentences.zh: 节目由丽莎·托宾剪辑，包含切尔西·丹尼尔、丹·鲍威尔和玛丽安·洛萨诺的原创音乐，由科里·施雷佩尔担任工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderland.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderland的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正准备迎接假期客人的到来。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会因为喝醉而睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线条件？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们是否有过敏症或食物敏感？
